---
title: "Direct and HB Realizations"
---

::: {.callout-warning}
## CONVERGING concept

This page explains the current candidate design. It does not define backend
rows, equations, supported inputs, or failure behavior; the linked contracts
remain the sole authority.
:::

## Design pressure

Direct analysis and harmonic balance answer related questions with different
representations and capabilities. Treating either backend as the circuit
authority would either distort the public circuit model or conceal a real
capability difference.

## Selected abstraction {#direct-and-hb-selected-network}

Both paths realize the same expanded Plan, component identities, Port
attachments, and selected view. SCNSim owns the public topology and network
meaning; Direct and HB are distinct realizations of it. The selected-view
S/Y/Z families provide a common analysis surface, while each Result keeps its
own evidence rather than pretending that Direct and HB are interchangeable
objects.

The same separation applies to Ports: one logical boundary has two auditable
backend lowerings, not two user-facing Port definitions.

## Problem solved

The model author can ask comparable network questions of one circuit without
re-authoring it for a solver. Differences that matter remain visible: Direct
uses the candidate's small-signal treatment for nonlinear elements, HB keeps
its nonlinear realization, and some physical content has a narrower HB
capability. This avoids silently weakening a Plan merely to make it portable.

## Intentionally not owned

This concept does not make JosephsonCircuits the topology authority, invent a
fake Direct backend marker, imply arbitrary bias-point linearization, or claim
that every Direct-capable Plan is HB-capable. It also does not force Direct and
HB onto one frequency grid. Each request owns its native grid; presentation may
overlay them without interpolation, while numerical comparison is limited to
explicit typed scalar Quantities.
